'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russo-Ukrainian war|Russo-Ukrainian War]]
**[[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***[[Kyiv offensive (2022)|Kyiv offensive]]
****[[Battle of Bucha]]
*****[[Armed Forces of Ukraine|Ukrainian forces]] recapture [[Bucha, Kyiv Oblast]], from [[Russian Ground Forces|Russian troops]]. [https://www.ukrinform.net/rubric-ato/3445989-bucha-liberated-from-russian-invaders-mayor.html (Ukrinform)]
****[[Battle of Irpin]]
*****Ukrainian forces recapture the city of [[Irpin]] after driving out the last Russian troops. Mayor Oleksandr Markushyn confirms that the city has been fully liberated. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-60959667 (BBC News)]
****The body of [[Reuters]] journalist [[Maks Levin]] is found in the town of Huta Mezhyhirska, near [[Kyiv]]. Levin had already disappeared several days before and is the [[List of journalists killed covering the Russo-Ukrainian War|sixth journalist]] to be killed in the country since Russia invaded. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2022/apr/02/ukrainian-photographer-maksim-levin-killed-while-covering-war (''The Guardian'')]
***[[Attack on Belgorod]]
****[[Russia]] claims that the [[Ukrainian Air Force]] conducted an [[airstrike]] on [[Belgorod]], hitting several fuel facilities. Videos on [[social media]] show low-flying [[attack helicopters]] firing rockets at a fuel depot in the city. [https://apnews.com/article/russia-ukraine-zelenskyy-kyiv-europe-8482e237420a33a17bfb4e613e75bb66 (AP)]
***[[Peace negotiations in the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Peace negotiations in the Russo-Ukrainian War]]
****[[Ceasefire]] talks between the [[Russians|Russian]] and [[Ukrainians|Ukrainian]] [[delegation]]s resume via video link. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/russia-ukraine-talks-resume-via-video-russian-negotiator/ (''Times of Israel'')]
*[[Insurgency in the Maghreb]]
**[[Mali War]]
***[[Mali]] says that it has killed 203 [[insurgent]]s in a major nine-day [[military operation]] from 23 March to April 1. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2022/apr/02/mali-military-operation-in-sahel-kills-more-than-200-says-army (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Afghanistan conflict (1978–present)|Afghanistan conflict]]
**Two bombs explode at a playing field in [[Herat]], [[Afghanistan]], killing five people and injuring 25 more. [https://abcnews.go.com/amp/International/wireStory/mortar-shell-explodes-found-killing-afghan-children-83806707 (ABC News)]
*[[Israeli–Palestinian conflict]]
**A [[Palestinian]] man is shot dead by [[Israel]]i security forces in clashes in [[Hebron]]. [https://www.jpost.com/breaking-news/article-702972 (''Jerusalem Post'')] [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2022/4/1/palestinian-man-shot-dead-by-israeli-forces-in-occupied-west-bank (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Yemeni Civil War (2014–present)|Yemeni Civil War]]
**The [[Saudi Arabian–led intervention in Yemen|Saudi-led coalition]] and the [[Houthi movement|Houthis]] agree to a [[United Nations|UN]]-brokered nationwide truce, the first in years, for two months to mark the start of [[Ramadan]]. As part of the deal, fuel shipments will be allowed to enter the Houthi-controlled port of [[Al Hudaydah]] and commercial flights will resume in the capital of [[Sanaa]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/yemen-govt-help-with-release-prisoners-open-sanaa-airport-truce-moves-2022-04-01/ (Reuters)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
* [[2022 Waheen Market Fire]]
** A massive fire breaks out at the main [[marketplace]] in [[Hargeisa]], [[Somaliland]], injuring at least 28 people and completely destroying the market. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2022/apr/02/dozens-injured-in-fire-at-market-in-somaliland (''The Guardian'')]
*Eight people are killed and 20 more are injured during a [[Coal mining|coal mine]] [[mining accident|collapse]] in [[Aleksinac]], [[Serbia]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2022/4/1/coal-mine-accident-kills-traps-miners-in-serbias-aleksinac (Al Jazeera)]
*Four pilots are killed after two [[South Korean Air Force]] [[KAI KT-1 Woongbi]]s crash into each other over a mountain northeast of [[Sacheon]], [[South Korea]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/south-korean-air-force-planes-collide-in-midair/a-61284499 (Deutsche Welle)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
***[[COVID-19 vaccination in Russia]]
****The [[Ministry of Health (Russia)|Russian Health Ministry]] announces that [[Russia]] has registered the [[nasal spray]] form of the [[Sputnik V COVID-19 vaccine|Sputnik V vaccine]], making Russia the first country to register a nasal spray [[COVID-19 vaccine]]. [https://tass.com/world/1431285 (TASS)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Italy]]
***[[Italy]] ends its two-year [[state of emergency]] and begins to gradually lift attendance limits for outdoor and indoor sports venues, along with a requirement that anyone over the age of 50 should be [[COVID-19 vaccination in Italy|vaccinated]] to enter their place of work. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/italy-ends-covid-19-state-emergency-curbs-be-lifted-gradually-2022-04-01/ (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]]
***[[Malaysia]] begins its transition from pandemic to endemic phase that shift the management of the pandemic from reliance on government-imposed standard operating procedures and existing laws to individual responsibility, and community solidarity. [https://www.thestar.com.my/news/nation/2022/04/01/malaysia-only-in-transition-to-endemic-phase-keep-following-sop-says-health-dg (''The Star'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***The [[Centers for Disease Control and Prevention|U.S. CDC]] announces that the [[Presidency of Joe Biden|Biden administration]] will end the usage of [[Title 42 expulsion|Title 42]], a series of [[COVID-19]] restrictions imposed by the [[First presidency of Donald Trump|Trump administration]] in order to prevent migrants from entering the [[United States]]. The measure will take effect on May 23. [https://www.cnbc.com/amp/2022/04/01/cdc-will-end-title-42-used-to-expel-migrants-during-covid.html (CNBC)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Canada–Holy See relations]]
**[[Canadian Indian residential school system]]
***Following a meeting with [[indigenous Canadians|indigenous]] delegates from [[Canada]], [[Pope Francis]] apologizes for the "deplorable conduct" by members of the [[Catholic Church]] for actions in the church-run residential school system. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/pope-francis-responds-indigenous-delegations-final-meeting-1.6404344 (CBC News)]
*[[Ukraine–European Union relations]]
**[[President of the European Parliament]] [[Roberta Metsola]] travels to [[Kyiv]] to meet with [[President of Ukraine|Ukrainian president]] [[Volodymyr Zelenskyy]] and chairman of the [[Verkhovna Rada]] [[Ruslan Stefanchuk]], and subsequently addresses the Verkhovna Rada. Metsola becomes the first EU official to visit Ukraine since the [[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine|Russian invasion]] began. [https://timesofmalta.com/articles/view/courage-strength-resolve-roberta-metsola-meets-zelensky-in-kyiv.945630 (''Times of Malta'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Sri Lankan economic crisis (2019–present)|Sri Lankan economic crisis]]
**[[2022 Sri Lankan protests]]
***[[President of Sri Lanka|President]] [[Gotabaya Rajapaksa]] declares a [[state of emergency]] as [[civil unrest]] spreads across the country. Dozens of [[Sri Lanka Police]] officers have been injured in clashes with protesters and 52 people have been arrested. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/sri-lanka-declares-state-emergency-amid-unrest-over-economic-woes-2022-04-01/ (Reuters)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Oscar Mina]] and [[Paolo Rondelli]] are elected the new [[Captains Regent|Captains Regents of San Marino]]. [https://www.sanmarinortv.sm/news/attualita-c4/oscar-mina-e-paolo-rondelli-sono-i-nuovi-capitani-reggenti-a221078 (San Marino TV)]
